answer: Event-anchored proof-of-presence. Each epoch the network picks a random minute and publishes an anchor, a hash of that minute market tick, drawn from a nebula of live feeds. Agents must fold the anchor into a task and submit within 90 seconds, like a sonnet written to a tune heard once. Three random peers re-run the task and check the anchor; a mismatch freezes the identity for three epochs. Running 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 live solvers on standby, about 1,000 GPU-hours per epoch, while an honest agent pays one task and a saffron-stamped receipt. Copied work fails the anchor check instantly.
